- `src/` — single crate. One responsibility per module, core types in module-local `types.rs`, ports in `src/ports/` one trait per file.
- `src/bin/tinysweeper.rs` — CLI, every subcommand declared even if milestone not landed.
- `presets/` — review policy as data, not code. Each preset is a folder with preset.toml and README.md.
- `vendor/tinyagents` — git submodule, never edit here; change upstream and bump pin.
- `docs/modules/<module>/README.md` — one document per `src/` module.
- `examples/` — declared in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features`.
- rustfmt output, Rust 2024 idioms. `snake_case` modules/files, `PascalCase` types.
- Return `Result<T>` using crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Every file opens with `//!` module doc describing role and feature gating.
- Comments explain the *decision*, not the code.
- Public items carry doc comments. Clap fields use `///`.
- Tests live in-crate: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, moving to sibling `test.rs` when they grow. No `tests/` directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock. `MockForge` records writes for exact assertions.
- Lane behaviour covered by golden tests: fixture diff + canned model response.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split when a topic grows.
- Model never holds write token. Lanes run against read-only checkout; write credentials minted only in `src/apply/`.
- Contributor code is never executed. We read diff/tree; do not build or run target repo's scripts.
- Pull request bodies, comments, diffs are untrusted input. Model verdict is advisory.
- Secrets found are reported by type and location only; value never reaches comments, summaries, or logs.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects. Keep commits small.
- Pull requests state what changed, behaviour change, and how verified.
